findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Correct the disposition-rule fixture mapping: e6a0-ba9b satisfies via signal (b) (its supersession is a comment, not a supersedes/duplicates link), reserving 'via (a)' for c8ed-d52d which carries a real supersedes→ecc7 link — and state that signal (a) covers only graph-recorded supersedes/duplicates while comment/description-recorded supersession falls to signal (b).
evidence: Plan: 'a supersedes or duplicates link (either direction) connecting the bug to the epic subtree or to a named successor ticket'
Plan fixture mapping: 'e6a0 satisfies via (a) (superseded by epic 4702 trail); … c8ed via (a) (supersedes the investigation epic)'
show_ticket e6a0-ba9b: deps = [{relation:'relates_to',target:'5fd2-…'}]; supersession is a COMMENT ('Superseded by epic 4702-a55c-7aeb-445a'); NO supersedes/duplicates link exists
show_ticket c8ed-d52d: deps include {relation:'supersedes',target:'ecc7-eee7-9341-4f6d'} — a real link, so (a) applies here but NOT to e6a0
findings.finding: The disposition-rule signal (a) — 'a supersedes or duplicates LINK (either direction) connecting the bug to the epic subtree or to a named successor ticket' — is inconsistent with the plan's own fixture mapping and misses the common prose-supersession case: fixture e6a0-ba9b records its supersession as a COMMENT ('Superseded by epic 4702-a55c-7aeb-445a…') and carries NO supersedes/duplicates link in its deps (only relates_to→5fd2), yet the plan asserts 'e6a0 satisfies via (a)'. By contrast c8ed-d52d does carry a real supersedes→ecc7 link, so it genuinely satisfies via (a). As specified, e6a0 can only satisfy via signal (b) (reasoned prose), so an implementer encoding the stated mapping ('e6a0 satisfies via (a)') would write a regression assertion that cannot hold against the store, and the link-based signal (a) will systematically fail to recognize dispositions recorded as prose rather than as a graph edge.
findings.location: Approach, stage-3 disposition rule + 'Fixture mapping' clause; Testing (must-pass e6a0-ba9b 'disposition trail: filed then superseded by epic 4702')
scenarios: Any deferred bug whose supersession/duplication is recorded in a comment or description (the incentive the plan wants to protect) rather than via `rebar link` — signal (a) never fires; only signal (b)'s prose-substance judgement can save it
The regression test 'e6a0 satisfies via signal (a)' fails because no supersedes/duplicates link exists in the fixture
findings.suggested_fix: Reclassify e6a0 as a signal-(b) fixture (substantive supersession prose in a comment) and keep c8ed as the signal-(a) fixture; add an explicit note that a supersession recorded only as prose is intentionally handled by (b), not (a).

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State how the verifier's disposition adjudication is validated over the must-pass/must-block fixtures: either extend the live calibration AC to cover the real verifier block/pass decision end-to-end, or document that the fake verdict map faithfully mirrors the disposition rule and pin the disposition-substance judgment to a named live check.
evidence: Plan: 'All regression/unit tests drive the screen through a FAKE forced-choice verdict map (deterministic, no live model)'
Plan: the live AC proves 'the real model -> epic_bug_screen_verdict validator path end-to-end' — scoped to the screen validator, not the verifier's block/pass disposition adjudication
Fixture mapping (e6a0 via (a), 30d3 via (b), c8ed via (a)) is a verifier-side disposition decision made through show_ticket, distinct from the screen's A/B/C verdict
E5 proxy-validation: the disposition adjudication is the defaulted risky path; offline-only coverage of it lets must-pass/must-block close green without the real disposition logic ever running
findings.finding: The verifier's disposition adjudication (block only an undispositioned deliverable-defect; SATISFY via supersedes/duplicates link or reasoned pre-existence prose) is the core novel behavior that separates the must-block fixtures (30a2, 5b09) from the must-pass fixtures (30d3 prose, e6a0 link, c8ed link) — but the plan states automated tests 'drive the screen through a FAKE forced-choice verdict map' and the sole live acceptance criterion covers only the screen's A/B/C -> epic_bug_screen_verdict validator path, not the live verifier's disposition decision over those fixtures. If both the screen verdict and the verifier verdict are faked, the must-block/must-pass regression assertions validate only plumbing while the disposition rule — the riskiest new logic — never runs as it will in production.
findings.location: Testing section ('All regression/unit tests drive the screen through a FAKE forced-choice verdict map ... the live haiku path is exercised only in manual calibration runs') and AC line 9 ([operator-attested] live calibration run 'proving the real model -> epic_bug_screen_verdict validator path')
scenarios: A regression run passes with a faked verifier verdict, but the live verifier's prose-substance judgment misclassifies 30d3 (blocks a legitimate deferral) or 5b09 (passes a real deliverable defect) — undetected because the automated suite never exercised the live disposition decision
findings.suggested_fix: Add an acceptance criterion that the live calibration run also records the verifier's block/pass outcome per fixture (proving 30d3/e6a0/c8ed pass and 30a2/5b09 block through the real disposition rule), keeping the automated suite on the fake map for the screen only.

evidence: 1 criterion line(s) bundle multiple deliverables with 'and' (split so each is independently verifiable).
findings.suggested_fix: Split compound criteria, replace subjective terms with observable outcomes, and state how each is verified.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Name the inbound-edge read the DET floor and the 'both directions' candidate traversal ride (e.g. reducer/_inbound.find_inbound_relationships) so the load-bearing reverse-link discovery — the direction where directional caused_by/supersedes/duplicates edges are actually stored — is explicit rather than assumed.
evidence: graph/_links.py + _commands/unlink.py: 'duplicates, supersedes, discovered_from, caused_by are directional (no reciprocal link)'
graph/_graph.py build_dep_graph: deps = list(state.get('deps', [])) — the ticket's OWN outbound links only
reducer/_inbound.find_inbound_relationships exists ('which other tickets point at this one?') but is not cited anywhere in the plan's Scope or Approach
Plan cites event_metrics._event_files (timing) and operations.assemble_context (context) but no inbound/reverse-link read
findings.finding: The inbound/reverse-link read that both the DET floor and the candidate filter depend on is unnamed, while the plan names only outbound-facing reads. The DET floor must find open bugs whose `caused_by` points at the epic or a descendant, but `caused_by` is a directional relation stored on the bug (no reciprocal), so the epic/descendant side has no outbound record of it; compiled-state `deps[]` (build_dep_graph → state.get('deps')) is outbound-only. Likewise stage-2's 'linked any-relation any-depth BOTH directions' requires reading inbound edges. A read primitive for this exists (reducer/_inbound.find_inbound_relationships, a byte-scan candidate superset then structured confirmation), but the plan cites event_metrics._event_files, graph, and assemble_context and never states how inbound edges are enumerated — leaving the load-bearing discovery mechanism unspecified.
findings.location: Approach stages 1 (DET floor 'caused_by -> epic or any descendant') and 2 ('linked any-relation/any-depth to the epic subtree, both directions')
scenarios: Implementer tries to satisfy the DET floor by reading the epic's own deps and finds no caused_by edges there (they live on the bugs), and either reinvents a full-corpus scan or narrows the floor incorrectly
Stage-2 'both directions' silently degrades to outbound-only because the inbound half was never wired

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State the epic_bug_screen_verdict normalizing validator's default: a malformed/out-of-vocabulary forced-choice value normalizes to a NON-surfacing verdict (B or C), matching the screen's degrade-open posture — do not inherit a first-member/surfacing default from the overlap_verdict idiom.
evidence: Plan: 'a new epic_bug_screen_verdict schema registered in contracts.py ... forced choice A/B/C + one-line citation ... with a normalizing validator; no hand-rolled JSON parsing.'
contracts.py:191-196 — the cited overlap_verdict validator defaults out-of-vocab to `related_distinct` (the NON-surfacing relation): `return r if r in allowed else "related_distinct"`.

Plan stance: 'Screen failure degrades open (log + skip), never blocks the close by itself' — but a validator that defaulted a garbled verdict to A (the surfacing value) would forward a candidate, contradicting degrade-open.
A/B verdicts drive whether a candidate is forwarded to the verifier as an A-verdict block candidate; the enum's malformed-value handling therefore affects the block path.
findings.finding: The new epic_bug_screen_verdict schema is specified with 'a normalizing validator' (overlap_verdict idiom) but the plan never states what an out-of-vocabulary or malformed forced-choice verdict normalizes TO — and unlike the overlap_verdict idiom it copies (whose default `related_distinct` is the non-surfacing/safe value), here verdict A is the surfacing/block-driving value, so the default direction is load-bearing.
findings.location: Approach stage 3 / Scope: 'src/rebar/llm/reviewers/epic_bug_screen.md (new prompt, outputs: epic_bug_screen_verdict) + src/rebar/llm/contracts.py (schema + normalizing validator, overlap_verdict idiom)'
scenarios: Haiku returns a malformed/empty/near-miss verdict token (e.g. 'a)', 'Option A', 'defect'); the normalizing validator must resolve it to a concrete A/B/C value.
A copied overlap-style validator that defaults to the FIRST enum member (A) would surface a candidate on garbled output, fail-toward-block rather than the plan's stated degrade-open.
findings.suggested_fix: Specify that the validator coerces any value not in {A,B,C} to C (unrelated) — the non-surfacing default — so a garbled screen output degrades open (never forwards an A-candidate), mirroring how overlap_verdict defaults to its non-surfacing `related_distinct`.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State an explicit enforced ceiling (or ordering/truncation rule) on the number of candidates the screen itself evaluates, distinct from the 8-candidate forwarding cap.
evidence: 'one warm call then parallel fan-out' — no cap named on the screen fan-out itself
'Backtested fan-out: median 3, p90 11, max 24 (upper bounds — snapshot compaction inflates)' — observed, not enforced
the cap 8 is described only for forwarding to the verifier
findings.finding: The forwarding cap (8 candidates to the verifier) is specified, but the haiku SCREEN itself runs one call per candidate over the full filtered fan-out (backtested median 3, p90 11, max 24) with no stated enforced ceiling — the observed max is descriptive, not a bound. A pathological epic with many filtered candidate bugs yields unbounded per-close haiku calls.
scenarios: An epic with dozens of open/in_progress candidate bugs in-window triggers dozens of parallel haiku calls at close
findings.suggested_fix: Add an AC/design note capping screen fan-out (e.g. evaluate at most N candidates, oldest/most-linked first) so per-close haiku calls are bounded.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State explicitly that the completion verifier's block-on-undispositioned-deliverable-defect verdict is a hard-blocking tier for the two must-block cases (which the DET floor cannot catch), and reconcile that with the 'screen never blocks alone / DET floor is the hard tier' statement.
evidence: 'the DET floor is the hard tier' vs 'Known-limited standalone coverage (caused_by edges are mostly auto-derived...)' — the floor likely misses 30a2/5b09
'Forward A-verdicts to the completion verifier... blocks only a defect-in-deliverable with NO recorded disposition'
must-block: 30a2-4f2a, 5b09-4f3d
findings.finding: The plan states 'Screen failure degrades open (log + skip), never blocks the close by itself; the DET floor is the hard tier,' but the two must-block regression cases (30a2, 5b09) are precisely the ones the DET floor is described as 'known-limited' on (caused_by edges rarely present on open orphans). The only path that hard-blocks those cases is the verifier acting on a forwarded A-verdict — yet the verifier is never named as a blocking tier, creating tension about which stage actually enforces the must-block outcome.
findings.location: Approach (stage 3 / disposition rule) vs Testing (must-block set)
scenarios: Implementer reads 'screen never blocks alone' and does not wire the verifier verdict to actually fail the close, so the two must-block cases silently pass
findings.suggested_fix: Clarify: the SCREEN (haiku) degrades open, but the VERIFIER acting on a forwarded A-verdict can and must block; map each must-block fixture (30a2, 5b09) to the stage that blocks it.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Specify that the forwarding cap (8) is a single named constant/config value rather than an inline literal, so post-calibration tuning is a one-line change.
evidence: 'cap 8 with titles-only overflow count' — magnitude stated, configurability not
findings.finding: The forwarding cap (8) and the 4096-token cache floor are numeric thresholds embedded in the design, but the plan does not say whether the forwarding cap is a named/configurable constant. A soon-to-tune gate threshold hardcoded inline is a maintainability risk.
findings.location: Approach ('cap 8 with titles-only overflow count') / Scope (epic_bug_screen.py)
scenarios: Calibration reveals 8 is too low/high and the value must be changed in several call sites

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Enumerate the DET floor's enforcement edit in completion_precheck (gate_ops.py): state how the floor's blocking bugs reach the run_verify=False short-circuit (extend child_closure_findings' `blocking` list vs. a new precheck branch) and how the AC-1 'fix / re-parent / dispute link' teaching message is produced instead of deterministic_child_failure's 'direct child' summary.
evidence: The BLOCK short-circuit is orchestrated in completion_precheck (gate_ops.py:62-74): it reads `blocking, uncertified = child_closure_findings(...)`, and only a non-empty `blocking` produces `run_verify=False` + `deterministic_child_failure(...)` (the no-LLM FAIL).
gate_ops.py module docstring (:14-18) states the child-closure short-circuit is modelled as the branch ELSE arm; a floor that does not feed `blocking`/`run_verify=False` will NOT block the close.

deterministic_child_failure (completion.py:242-260) hard-codes a 'direct child ticket(s) are not closed' summary, whereas AC-1 requires a distinct 'fix / re-parent / dispute link' teaching message for the caused_by floor — implying either an extended child_closure_findings return or a new precheck branch, which the plan does not name.
Scope lists gate_ops.py ONLY for context-append ('no output-schema change'); the enforcement wiring for the floor is absent from both the completion.py and gate_ops.py scope lines.
findings.finding: The DET caused_by floor's ENFORCEMENT (the deterministic short-circuit BLOCK that skips the LLM) requires wiring into completion_precheck in src/rebar/llm/workflow/gate_ops.py, but the plan's Scope assigns gate_ops.py only the 'append compact candidates into the fenced context' task and assigns completion.py only the floor/candidate-filter logic — leaving the enforcement path unenumerated.
findings.location: Scope: 'src/rebar/llm/completion.py (DET floor ...)' and 'src/rebar/llm/workflow/gate_ops.py (completion_precheck: append compact candidates ...)'; Approach stage 1
scenarios: An epic close with an open caused_by bug in its subtree: if the floor is computed in completion.py but not surfaced into completion_precheck's blocking/run_verify=False path, the close is NOT blocked (AC-1 unmet) despite the logic existing.
Implementer edits completion.py only and assumes gate_ops.py needs no enforcement change (per Scope), shipping a floor that silently no-ops at the gate.
findings.suggested_fix: Add gate_ops.py's completion_precheck to Scope as an enforcement edit (not just context-append): either have child_closure_findings also return caused_by-floor blockers (so the existing blocking branch blocks) with a dedicated floor finding whose message carries the fix/re-parent/dispute-link guidance, or add a distinct precheck branch that emits a FAIL verdict via a new floor-specific message helper; name whichever path in Scope.
